title: What your accent says about you
text: Accent discrimination is one of the last openly tolerated prejudices, according to sociolinguists. Job applicants with regional accents are still routinely judged as less {{1}} than those who sound 'neutral', despite the absence of any connection between accent and ability. The bias begins astonishingly early: children as young as five prefer to befriend speakers of high-status accents. Historically, broadcasters were required to adopt standard pronunciation, a rule that survived until the 1970s and whose {{2}} still shapes hiring in some industries. Researchers note that accent prejudice is really class prejudice by {{3}}, since accents map tightly onto social geography. Changing an accent is possible, but many refuse, {{4}} the cost as too high to their sense of identity. Increasingly, employers are being urged to treat accent the way they treat race or gender — as a characteristic on which no judgement of {{5}} can rest. Some organisations now train interviewers to notice their own reactions. Progress, linguists caution, will be slow: accents evolve constantly, and with them the {{6}} for prejudice. But the direction of travel is clear, and the days of the single 'proper' way to sound appear to be {{7}}. What remains is a simple test: if the words are right, the voice should not {{8}}.

gaps.explanation: 'judged as less capable' — able to do the job; availability, cost and punctuality are not what accent prejudice is about.
'whose legacy still shapes hiring' — lasting influence; remains, ruins and residues are physical leftovers.
judging the cost as too high — judge + object + as + adjective; deem drops the 'as', and grading and scoring are for tests.
'no judgement of competence' — the ability the job requires; compassion, compliance and posture are not hiring criteria.
'the targets for prejudice' — what prejudice directs itself at; purposes, venues and stages are not its objects.
'their days are numbered' — the fixed idiom; tally, list and schedule do not form it.
'the voice should not matter' — be important; concern and apply would need different patterns, and arrive misses the point.
